cs: Assets/Scripts/Flight/PlaneModelFrame.cs (NEW) + Flight/PlaneCockpitBaker.cs, PlaneCockpitMeasurement.cs, PlaneHallFill.cs, PlaneController.cs, PlanePropellers.cs, PlanePhysics.cs, FlightModel.cs; Combat/AirframeBreakup.cs, Combat/PlaneDamage.cs; Editor/BuildPlayableScene.cs, Editor/BuildFlyableScene.cs; Props/WarehouseCraneFill.cs (comment only)
note:
THE BIGGEST VISIBLE BUG (docs/QUALITY_BAR.md) closed: the aeroplane the player flies no longer points its tail along the thrust vector. covers:0 BY ARITHMETIC, not by modesty -- src/planes.js is at 1614/1614 claimed, 0 free, so src/planes.js:813-836 makePlaneModel's straightening tail and :1528-1540 makeGameplayPlane's wrapper/group nesting are reported in prose here rather than billed. Nothing in this entry adds a line of coverage; it makes already-billed lines actually RUN, which is this port's signature failure mode.

WHAT WAS WRONG. PlaneDef.YawUnity/RollUnity had zero Transform consumers and the model child was parented at IDENTITY in all four places a plane gets built, so (a) the straightened nose stayed on -Z while Flight/FlightModel.cs thrusts along plane.forward = +Z, and (b) the 9 defs that carry an orientation fix were never straightened at all.

THE FIX IS ONE CHAIN, THREE NODES, because three different frames are genuinely needed and collapsing any two re-creates the bug:
  planeRoot            FLIGHT frame, nose +Z (FlightModel, Combat/Guns.cs's MuzzleLocal z=+3.65, Combat/Rockets.cs's pylon z=+0.9 -- the port ALREADY assumed +Z everywhere except the art)
   model_frame         localRotation = 180 deg about Y == src/planes.js's `wrapper` space, nose -Z. Every -Z-anchored measurement runs in here.
    model_scale        localScale = def.Scale == the JS's `group` (planes.js:1537); it must sit BELOW model_frame because a node's own scale does not appear in its own local space, and findCockpit measures the wrapper AFTER the scale.
     model_file        localRotation = YawUnity/RollUnity == the JS's `fixed` group (planes.js:834). Its own local space is the FILE frame, which is byte-identical to the frame PlaneProps/PropellerSystem always ran in -- which is why PROPSUM stays 31/31 with the same radii and the same hinted hubs.
      model            the FBX/OBJ at its NATURAL import transform (t28.fbx is rot (270.02,0,0) / scale 100 -- never reset).
The recentre (planes.js:830 'pivot on the AIRFRAME') is applied PRE-ROTATED to model_file.localPosition = -(fix*centre) rather than to the model, because fix*(v-c) == fix*v - fix*c but only the first leaves model_file's own origin at the FILE origin. Putting it on the model (the literal JS transcription) moved the Cessna 310's two hand-measured propHubs off their geometry and took the bake from 31 propellers to 29.

SITES HANDED THE MODEL FRAME (not sign-flipped by hand): PlaneCockpitBaker.Bake measures/builds in model_frame and converts the seat back through PlaneModelFrame.ModelPointToRoot (the frame's REAL orientation, not a hard-coded sign); PlaneCockpitKit's kit/box-shell/hood are children of model_frame so their hand-authored z offsets still mean what they say; PlaneProps via PlanePropellers.ModelRoot = model_file; PlaneHallFill measures the STRAIGHTENED box vertex-precisely (planes.js:1530's own 'precise=true' rationale -- Renderer.bounds inflates under tornado/tu144/neonfly's rotations).
SITES WHOSE Z COMPARISON REVERSES ONCE, inline and cited: PlanePhysics's five ground-contact stations (planephys.js:257-266) and TearAt's tail line; Combat/AirframeBreakup's four structural regions and its TailZ/NoseZ (breakup.js:63-71); Combat/PlaneDamage's _partAt, the shot-off-wing cut line and the smoke plume station.
UNTOUCHED, PROVEN: PlaneController.BellyOffset = -BoxOf(...).min.y -- a 180 deg yaw about Y cannot change min.y, so WHEEL_HEIGHT and touchdown are bit-identical. The crane's slung P-51 deliberately stays in the MODEL frame (it has no PlaneController, no flight frame, a NoBoardMarker, and WarehouseCrane.PlaneYaw is hand-authored against a -Z nose); its hub is still onNose=1.

TWO TOLERANCE-FREE PROOFS that the frame is right, both from numbers the runtime had no way to know:
  * the P-51's authored spinner station (src/planes.js:239 propMake.hub = [0,1.57,4.95]) now measures propZ=+4.95 in the flight frame on a +-5.34 m airframe. The first GPU render measured it at hubLocalToPlane=(0.00,1.57,-4.95) with planeForward=(0,0,1): the hero's propeller was on its tail.
  * f4f's src/planes.js:212 `cockpit: { z: -1.8 }` override now lands at seatZmodel=-1.80 exactly. A negative z override only means anything measured along a STRAIGHTENED -Z-nose axis, and f4f's file is stored nose-WEST -- which is why f4f was the one `cockpit=insane` of 35 before this change and is sane now.
PACKING: ORIENTPACK id=cessna310 before=9.88x11.20 after=11.20x9.88 (published 11.25x9.74); id=f4f before=8.15x11.60 after=11.60x8.15 (published 11.58x8.76). PlaneHallFill's `Span = size.x, Len = size.z` is finally the real span and length.
NOTHING THAT MUST NOT MOVE MOVED, same editor launch (PlaneOrientProbe.Suite chains them): AXISSUM planes=35 noseNegZ=29 nosePosZ=3 noseOther=3 spanAlongX=32 cockpitSane=34 (the untouched control -- it measures the RAW assets, which did not change); PROPSUM planes=15 found=31 want=31 missing=0; CRANEFILL_PROPNOSE hubZ=-4.950 onNose=1 authoredHubF=4.950; AIRBOX id=spitfire bellyOffset=-0.469 and TOUCHDOWN id=spitfire bellyAfter=100.000 diff=0.0000 pass=true.

notPorted:
TWO AIRFRAMES THE MEASUREMENT CANNOT ADJUDICATE, and they are ASSET/spec questions, not chain bugs -- the chain applies exactly src/planes.js:834's fix composed with one 180 deg yaw, so each of these points precisely where the Three.js build points it.
  * p100 -- its detected propeller is at +3.95 m on a +-4.44 m airframe (so, the nose) while both the end-slab rule and the canopy centroid put the nose at -Z. src/planes.js carries NO orientation fix for it and PlanePropsProbe.Axis independently flags it against the raw file (`AXISSUM unexplained=2 ids=p100:+Z`). Adding a yaw here would be a silent divergence from the reference implementation, so it is reported instead. Needs one look at a render.
  * hsp75 -- a canard PUSHER (its own src/planes.js description: 'frta ukan, sache tsin, khrakhni kudshi' = wing at the back, canard at the front, screw in the tail), so the 'widest end slab is the tail' rule is invalid for it by construction; its asset is also only 0.47x its published 18.0 m span. Its def's `yaw = PI` is applied faithfully.
ONE COCKPIT STILL UNMEASURED, with a cause rather than a shrug: tornado reads `cockpit=insane room=0.25 from="hull profile UNMEASURED"`, and ORIENTCKDIAG id=tornado candidates=0 says why -- the asset contains NO mesh whose name or material matches canopy/glass/cockpit/seat/window, so findCockpit has nothing to pick in the JS either and falls through to the hull profile, which gives 0.25 m against PilotRoomMin 0.30. Its earlier `sane` reading was taken across a 37.7-degree-skewed airframe, i.e. luck, not correctness. The parity-preserving fix is a one-line `cockpit: { z }` override in src/planes.js next to the nine that already exist ('the measurement found the fin, not the nose') -- a DATA change to the spec, deliberately not made unilaterally. So the sane set is 34/35 before and 34/35 after, with f4f fixed and tornado now honest.
Also not done: AirframeBreakup/PlaneDamage's reversed z comparisons have no probe of their own (the shot-off-wing path needs a live hit); and PlaneModelFrame.Ensure's adopt-the-existing-model branch is exercised only by a plane built outside the four known builders.

note: src/game.js:779 `if (rec.loose || rec.dead) return false` -- '...and not one that is tumbling through the air or burning on its back after somebody rammed it'. PlaneRecord.Loose is written by Flight/PlanePhysics (MakeLoose :553, Park :719) and had ZERO readers anywhere in the project, so Enter would board a wreck mid-tumble. One statement inside SwapToPlane, resolving the plane to its registry record through the existing TargetRegistry.RecOf (the same collider match PickAt uses) so nothing new has to know the registry's shape. Filed under a distinct `cs` string so the merge does not overwrite the base GameLoop.cs claim.
verified: Compiles clean and bakes clean in the same runs as the orientation entry (BuildPlayableScene.Run exit 0, no `error CS`). NOT separately probed: driving it needs a plane knocked loose by a ram and then an Enter in the same frame, which is a live-combat scenario no existing probe sets up -- the honest statement is that the gate is wired and the flag it reads is maintained (PlanePhysics.cs:553/:719), not that a probe has watched it refuse a boarding.
